newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bruton calls for signs of progress in EU.
newsitem.headline: Bruton calls for signs of progress in EU.

text.p: Irish Prime Minister John Bruton formally invited his European Union colleagues on Wednesday to this week's summit in Dublin, saying they must show that the bloc is on track for the future.
"We must demonstrate a commitment to advance the political and economic health of the Union," Bruton told fellow leaders in a letter, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters.
The summit is to be held on Friday and Saturday.
Bruton said the commitment should be shown by making "decisive progress" towards a new EU treaty, to be agreed in June next year, and on economic and monetary union (EMU) with its single EU currency.

Saying he hoped EU finance ministers meeting in Dublin on Thursday could reach agreement on a post-EMU budget pact, Bruton said the summit should endorse a report on how the single currency, the euro, will work.
The report covers the budget pact, the legal framework for the new currency and a new exchange rate mechanism for those currencies outside EMU.

"(We) must aim to endorse this report, and the actions proposed in it for the next phase of work, in order to intensify decisively the momentum for EMU to begin on 1 January, 1999," Bruton said in the letter.
Leaders will also be shown the first euro notes.
Bruton also called for the leaders to endorse a report on progress towards a new EU treaty.
"I would hope that the...draft could be seen as a good basis for further negotiations under the Netherlands presidency," he said.
The Netherlands takes over from Ireland as EU president on January 1.
